explanations: Amber is named after fossilised tree resin, a soft sticky sap that sometimes trapped insects and has been cut as a gemstone since antiquity.
Red is the colour of blood, long associated with danger and courage, and in much of Asia with happiness and good fortune.
Green is the traditional colour of safety and permission, and the hue many creatures take on as camouflage.
Red stops traffic, amber signals a change and green lets it go: the three usual colours of a traffic light, arranged in that order.

sources.excerpt: It has been appreciated for its color (orange, brown and, sometimes, red) and natural beauty since the Neolithic times, and worked as a gemstone since classical antiquity.
Because it originates as a soft, sticky tree resin, amber sometimes contains animal and plant material as inclusions.
Since red is the color of blood, it has historically been associated with sacrifice, danger, and courage.
In China, India, and many other Asian countries it is the color symbolizing happiness and good fortune.
Green is also the traditional color of safety and permission; a green light means go ahead, a green card permits permanent residence in the United States.
Many creatures have adapted to their green environments by taking on a green hue themselves as camouflage.
The usual traffic light colors are red to stop traffic, amber to signal a change, and green to allow traffic to proceed.
